title: Moon Water Winners: Students Invent Cool Ways to Drink in Space!
summary: Imagine you're an astronaut on the Moon. You're thirsty after a long moonwalk. But how do you get a drink when water is super precious and the equipment has to work in crazy cold space? That's the puzzle NASA asked college students to solve! In the 2026 Human Lander Challenge, teams from across the country designed systems to manage water and air inside future lunar landers. The winner? California Polytechnic State University, who scored a $10,000 prize for their 'Peltier-based Hydration Accumulation Terminal'—a fancy name for a device that uses special cooling plates to collect and give out water. Think of it like a super-high-tech water fountain that works in space! Purdue University came in second ($5,000) with an 'Enhanced Potable Water Dispenser,' and Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University got third ($3,000) for their 'Advanced Quality Orbital Rehydration Assembly.' All these inventions help astronauts stay safe and hydrated on long missions. NASA's Artemis program plans to land astronauts on the Moon in 2028, and these student ideas might actually be used in the next-generation landers. Natalie Martinez-Vlasoff from NASA said the students showed a strong understanding of how to make life support systems reliable. So next time you take a sip of water, think about how tricky it would be to design a cup that works in zero gravity—and on the Moon!
why_it_matters: Your school science projects today could lead to inventions that help astronauts drink water on the Moon tomorrow.
